chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sowli narrated to us; Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Nasr al-Razi narrated to me, on the authority of their fathers and Al-Husayn ibn Umar al-Akhbari, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Husayn, the scribe of Basha al-Kabeer, in the last two [days].

That Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) had a fever, so he decided to have phlebotomy performed. Al-Ma'mun rode [to see him]. He had previously said to his servant: 'Crush this with your hand,' referring to something he took out of a vase. The servant crushed it on a tray. Then he said: 'Stay with me and do not wash your hand.' He rode to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) and sat until he was phlebotomized in front of him. Ubaydullah said: 'Rather, he delayed the phlebotomy.' Al-Ma'mun said to that servant: 'Bring us that pomegranate.' The pomegranate was on a tree in the garden of Ar-Ridha's (peace be upon him) house. The servant picked it, then said: 'Sit.' He peeled it and crushed it in a bowl. Al-Ma'mun ordered it to be washed, then said to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Suck some of it.' He said: 'Until the Commander of the Faithful leaves.' He said: 'By God, no, unless in my presence. If I were not afraid my stomach would become moist, I would have sucked it with you.' So he sucked a few spoonfuls, and Al-Ma'mun left. I did not finish the afternoon prayer until Ar-Ridha had sat up fifty times.
Al-Ma'mun sent to him [saying]: 'I know that this is a fainting and lethargy due to the bloodletting in your body.' The matter worsened during the night, and he (peace be upon him) died by morning.

The last thing he spoke was: 'Say: If you had remained in your houses, those for whom death was decreed would certainly have gone forth to the places of their death... And it is the decree of Allah.' Al-Ma'mun rose early the next day and ordered his washing and shrouding. He walked behind his funeral procession barefoot and uncovered, saying: 'O brother, indeed Islam has been blemished by your death, and destiny overcame my estimation regarding you.' He opened the grave of Al-Rashid and buried him with him, saying: 'I hope that Allah, the Exalted, will benefit him by his proximity [to Ar-Ridha].'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida)

ai.seo_question: How did Al-Ma'mun poison and bury Imam Ar-Ridha according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* details the specific mechanism of Imam al-Rida’s martyrdom, where Caliph al-Ma'mun personally administered poison via a pomegranate and witnessed the Imam's gradual decline. The text highlights the political symbolism of al-Ma'mun burying the Imam beside his father, Harun al-Rashid, to legitimize Abbasid rule, while the Imam’s final recitation of Surah Al-Imran (3:154) underscores the inevitability of divine decree (*Qadr*) over human plotting.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 61-1 Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sowli quoted on the authority of Ubaydillah ibn Abdullah and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Nasr al-Razi, on the authority of his father and Al-Husayn ibn Umar al-Akhbari, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Husayn - the author of Bogha al-Kabeer - that in the last days of his life,

Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) got a fever. Then he decided to have a phlebotomy performed. Then Al-Ma’mun rode on (an animal) to see him. Before going there, he took out something from a vase and asked his servant to crush it with his hands. The servant crushed it on a tray. Al-Ma’mun told the servant that he does not have to wash his hands. Then he asked the servant to accompany him to Ar-Ridha’’s (a.s.) house. When Al-Ma’mun entered the house, he sat in front of the Imam (a.s.) until he (a.s.) decided to start the blood-letting. Or as Ubaydillah said he put off the blood-letting and told his servant to bring him a pomegranate. There was a pomegranate tree in the garden of Ar-Ridha’’s (a.s.) house.The servant picked a pomegranate from the tree. Al-Ma’mun asked him to peel it, open it up and prepare it for eating. The servant peeled it and prepared it in a bowl. Then Al-Ma’mun asked the servant to wash his hands. Then the servant brought in the pomegranate. Then Al-Ma’mun told Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.), ‘Have some.’ Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, ‘No, not until the Commander of the Faithful (Al-Ma’mun) leaves.’ Then Al-Ma’mun insisted on it by saying, ‘By God! It is not possible. You must eat some of it in my presence. I would also have some of it along with you were it not for my stomachache.’ Then Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) ate a few spoonfuls of it and Al-Ma’mun left. However Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) fainted and sat up again fifty times that day before saying the afternoon prayers.

Al-Ma’mun sent someone to Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) and said, ‘I know that this unconsciousness and feeling of apathy is due to the phlebotomy that you had done. However, Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) got worse at night, and died before the morning.

The following were the final words which he uttered, ‘…Say: Even if you had remained in your homes, those for whom death was decreed would certainly have gone forth to the place of their death…’ ‘And the command of God is a decree determined.’’ When the following morning came, Al-Ma’mun woke up early and ordered that Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) be washed and shrouded. He himself followed the corpse with a bare head and in bare and said, ‘O brother! Indeed there is a gap in Islam due to your demise. And God’s destiny (for you) overcame my efforts on your behalf.’ Then Al-Ma’mun had the grave of Harun Ar-Rashid (al-Ma’mun’s afther) dug open and buried Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) there. Then Al-Ma’mun said, ‘I hope that God the Highest would grant some benefits to my father due to being close to Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.).’”
